actions.description: On the status port, select robot 1 and halt. Confirms TrajState 0 or 1 only when every MoveJ this endpoint wrote has been answered, and this halt has read state after that. The reply follows the mailbox wait (Main.gpl:225). RapidDecel does not retire an unanswered command
actions.name: halt

outputs.description: TrajState after halt: 0 halted or 1 idle
outputs.name: traj_state

outputs.description: The state reply that showed 0 or 1
outputs.name: reply

facts.text: Startup declares Status1Port 10000 and Robot1Port 10100. StartMain opens the status port with TcpComMain(0, Status1Port) and TcpCom1 opens the robot port with TcpComMain(1, Robot1Port). The startup comment says a motion thread can block and the status thread does not
The status thread is robot 0 with IsStatus set, and after AcceptSocket it stops listening so the port serves one client
NewRobNum is applied at the start of the next receive, before that receive's bytes are read
A status command runs in the comm thread; a robot-port command is posted to the robot mailbox and the comm thread waits until the mailbox is clear
After Handler returns, the robot thread sets the mailbox to Nothing and wakes the comm thread
PC mode's default reply is 0
The client states that a response begins with 0 when the command was successful, or a negative error code
The PC-mode reply on the socket is Cmd.Reply followed by CR LF
halt calls Robot.RapidDecel for the command's robot and the comment says motion stops with power left on; the handler does not clear a destination
In PC mode, state replies 0 and the integer Robot.TrajState of the selected robot
TrajState labels are 0 Halted, 1 Idle, 2 to 6 position-mode motion, 8 velocity, 9 homing, 10 jog, 11 external trajectory and 15 motion terminated nulling
Check_ProfIdx rejects an index below 1 or above N_PROF; success leaves the reply unchanged
N_PROF is the constant 20
MoveJ takes a profile index and up to 12 angle parameters, calls Move.Loc when there are more parameters than axes, and does not change its reply to a reached flag
Joint angles are degrees for rotary axes and millimetres for linear axes
mspeed's optional parameter is the new system speed as a percentage and is stored in PDbNum 601; those lines state no numeric range
On the status thread, selectRobot requests NewRobNum for the given robot; selecting the current robot leaves the reply at the default
The command delegate is Cmd_ concatenated with the first token as received
stop_robot assigns halt and sends it through send_command
connect_robot connects to self.host and self.port
send_command receives with recv and that line does not call settimeout
The client states that a second command will not reply until the first motion is complete
A socket.error around socket() falls off the end of connect_robot. connect() is outside that handler, so its socket.error propagates. send_command returns the string failed on socket.error
The lab client's status-port init sends selectRobot 1 and then enable_power
The lab client's movement-state comment labels 0 as power off and 1 as stopping

measures.description: Robot 1 TrajState from one state command on the robot port (0 halted, 1 idle)
measures.name: traj_state

operator_required.name: move_joints
operator_required.reason: Cmd.gpl:116 rejects a profile index below 1 or above N_PROF, and Globals.gpl:82 sets N_PROF to 20. Those two numbers are not in one file, and one field cannot carry two limits, so the operator overlay supplies the profile bound. An undefined profile is a negative reply and is a failure.

operator_required.name: move_joints
operator_required.reason: mspeed takes the new system speed as a percentage (Cmd.gpl:532) and the GPL states no numeric range; tcp_driver.py:498's 0-100 is the client's comment, not a controller limit

safe_state.description: TrajState 0 or 1 with power still on, and only when this endpoint has no unanswered MoveJ; RapidDecel does not retire a mailbox command. The arm may hold or sag, and this package does not re-enable power, attach or home and offers no unpause
